sections.h2: Red Willow County at a glance
sections.html:
Red Willow County hugs Nebraska's southern border, and McCook is where the courthouse stands. Indianola is the other city. Bartley, Danbury and Lebanon are villages, while Marion, Perry and Shippee are unincorporated. The Republican River crosses the north-central part, and the low ground beside it is farmed.

The 2020 census counted 10,702 residents, and the 2025 estimate is 10,307, a drop of 3.7 percent. Numbers have slipped at every census since 1980. There are 4,532 households and 5,157 housing units, and 12.1% of the units were vacant. Roughly 71.8% of occupied homes are lived in by their owners.

After decades of slow loss, some owners would rather close quickly as-is than sit through a long listing. A vacant house still draws a tax bill, and it ages faster when nobody checks the roof, furnace and plumbing.

sections.h2: Who bills and collects the tax
sections.html:
Real estate tax is collected by the county treasurer at 502 Norris Avenue in McCook. Mail goes to PO Box 490, McCook, NE 69001, and the phone is 308-345-6515, extension 1. The state's tax portal shows current and back taxes and takes payment for both. A card costs 2.35 percent with a $2.00 minimum, and an e-check costs $2.00.

Next door in the same building, the assessor answers at 308-345-4388 or assessor@redwillowcountyne.gov, weekdays from 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m., with no lunch closure. That office values real and personal property, maintains the parcel maps, builds the tax roll the treasurer bills from, and fields questions about homestead exemption eligibility.

The assessor lists four things that push a value up or down: movement in the market, outside influences on the property, improvements added or removed, and a remodel or rehab. A new garage or finished basement raises the number, and tearing down a tired outbuilding should lower it.

Exemptions exist for educational and religious facilities and for qualifying seniors and people with disabilities. Ask the assessor's office which one fits before you assume you owe the full amount.

A protest has to reach the County Clerk by June 30. Say what value you want and why. The clerk mails the board's decision by August 2, and the Tax Equalization and Review Commission accepts appeals until August 24.

Give the board something concrete: a recent appraisal, photos and a bid for needed repairs, or sale prices of similar houses nearby.

sections.h2: How the March tax sale works
sections.html:
On the first Monday of March each year, the county sells certificates for unpaid real estate tax at the courthouse. The delinquent list is advertised in the local paper and online for three consecutive weeks in February.

  • The buyer pays the overdue tax, not the purchase price of the house, and carries later years' taxes as they come due.
  • Owners get three years to redeem, with the certificate earning 14 percent interest.
  • After three years with no redemption, the certificate holder has six months to start foreclosure.
  • Buyers pay $25 to register, and the county keeps $20 on each certificate sold.

The treasurer gives no legal advice to certificate buyers and points them to Nebraska statutes 77-1801 through 77-1941. If your own parcel is headed for the sale, talk with an attorney well before the last week.

At closing the title company requests the payoff from the treasurer, subtracts it from your proceeds and records the deed. If the parcel already went to the March sale, the certificate must be redeemed first, so ask the treasurer whether one exists before you set a date.

The register of deeds collects Nebraska's documentary stamp tax from you, the seller: $3.32 on every $1,000 of value for deeds recorded from July 18, 2026.

A cash sale avoids the lender's appraisal and repair demands, which helps with an older or vacant house. Send us the parcel number and we will walk through the numbers with you.

Three small jobs make every later conversation shorter. Find the parcel on the state tax portal and jot down what shows as owed. Ring the treasurer at 308-345-6515, extension 1, to check that figure and ask whether a certificate was ever sold on the parcel in March. If the valuation looks wrong, the assessor at 308-345-4388 can explain how it was reached, and protests close June 30.

Gather bids or photos for anything an inspector will flag, such as the roof, furnace or plumbing, and give the title company a list of open balances so the payoff is ready on signing day.

sections.h2: Owning a house that sits empty
sections.html:
With so many vacant units around the county, an empty house is not unusual here. It still costs money. The tax bill comes every year, and a freeze can burst a pipe in a home no one is watching.

Ask a neighbor or relative to look in regularly, keep payments current, and decide soon whether to list for months or to take a quick as-is offer. Cash buyers purchase in present condition, so a tired roof or an old furnace need not be repaired first.

Bank financing brings an appraisal, and an appraisal on a house needing work can derail a closing. Without a lender, those hurdles vanish and the calendar rests on the title search and on how quickly the tax payoff is confirmed.

The same obligations remain at the table: stamp tax, open tax balances, and the recorded deed. What shrinks is the waiting.

Have your parcel number, photo ID and newest tax statement nearby for calls and visits. An heir should bring documents showing authority to sign. If the property is unoccupied, mention that to the title company at the outset.

sections.h2: If your parcel is headed for the March sale
sections.html:
Timing is the whole game here. The list is advertised in February, so by the time your name or parcel shows up in the paper, the sale is only weeks away. Paying the overdue amount before the first Monday of March keeps the parcel off the block. Selling before then works too, because the title company pays the delinquent tax from proceeds.

Ask the treasurer for a current figure, since interest keeps adding to the balance. Buyers at the sale cover later years' taxes as they come due, which means an investor with a certificate is tied to your parcel for up to three years.

faqs.q: When do Red Willow County taxes become delinquent?
faqs.a: May 1 for the first half and September 1 for the second.

faqs.q: How do I protest my Red Willow County valuation?
faqs.a: Get a protest to the County Clerk by June 30, naming the value you want and your reasons. The Board of Equalization hears it, and the state commission handles further appeals.

faqs.q: Who do I call about a Red Willow County valuation?
faqs.a: The assessor, at 308-345-4388. The office is at 502 Norris Avenue in McCook, open weekdays from 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m.

faqs.q: Can I pay Red Willow County property tax by card?
faqs.a: Yes, on the tax portal, at 2.35 percent with a $2.00 minimum. An e-check costs $2.00, and a mailed payment goes to PO Box 490, McCook.

faqs.q: What is the Red Willow County tax sale?
faqs.a: A yearly sale of certificates for unpaid real estate tax, held the first Monday in March. Certificates earn 14 percent interest, and owners have a three-year redemption period.
